question:
The figure is a low-magnification pathology slide scan. Three uniform gray square test patches have been printed onto it at the normalized regions below ([x1, y1, x2, y2], origin top-left). At most one of the three patches has a gray value different from the other two — beware: the different surroundings can make identical grays appear different, and a real difference can be masked. Which patch has the different gray value?
(A) [0.8213, 0.1553, 0.8603, 0.2253]
(B) [0.6245, 0.3703, 0.6635, 0.4403]
(C) [0.7319, 0.8788, 0.7709, 0.9488]
(D) All three patches have exactly the same gray value.

Answer with only the correct option letter.

- Patch (B) is located at [0.6245, 0.3703, 0.6635, 0.4403]. This is in the middle of the rightmost quarter, roughly between 0.62 and 0.66 horizontally and 0.37 and 0.44 vertically.
- Patch (C) is located at [0.7319, 0.8788, 0.7709, 0.9488]. This is in the bottom-right corner of the rightmost quarter, roughly between 0.73 and 0.77 horizontally and 0.878 and 0.948 vertically.

</tool_call>

After cropping patch (A), I can see it is a uniform gray square. Now, I will crop patch (B) to compare.

Now that I have cropped all three patches into separate images ([img3], [img4], and [img5]), I can now compare them directly. To do this accurately, I will overlay them on the same background to ensure a fair comparison.
